query: How do review facets differ by sentiment label?

per_column.name: review_word_count
per_column.rationale: Review length is a plausible external facet that could differ by sentiment, but as a raw count it is very fine-grained (many singleton values). Without binning it supports comparison only weakly; interpretable as 'longer vs shorter' but not cleanly segmented.

per_column.name: review_sentence_count
per_column.rationale: Sentence count is an interpretable structural facet with a compact, well-populated range (mostly 2-8), so it can be grouped and compared against sentiment meaningfully.

per_column.name: exclamation_count
per_column.rationale: Exclamation usage is an intuitive expressive facet plausibly linked to sentiment. Distribution is near-constant zero but has a usable none/some contrast, allowing a meaningful segmentation.

per_column.name: question_count
per_column.rationale: Interpretable in principle, but 232/250 are zero — so near-constant that essentially no meaningful comparison across sentiment can be drawn.

per_column.name: caps_word_count
per_column.rationale: All-caps emphasis is an interpretable stylistic facet plausibly associated with strong sentiment; a none/some split is usable despite skew toward zero.

per_column.name: positive_word_count
per_column.rationale: Counting positive lexicon words is essentially a proxy for the sentiment label itself; it restates the focus rather than opening an external associational relationship.

per_column.name: negative_word_count
per_column.rationale: Like positive_word_count, this is a direct lexical proxy for sentiment and largely restates label_pos rather than providing an independent facet.

per_column.name: has_personal_pronoun
per_column.rationale: A clean binary facet (personal/impersonal framing) with a reasonable split (203/47), easily grouped and compared against sentiment.

per_column.name: avg_word_length
per_column.rationale: A near-constant continuous score clustered tightly around ~4.4 with fine-grained decimals; it is opaque and offers little separable structure for meaningful comparison.

judge.rationale: The set mixes genuinely useful, interpretable facets (sentence_count, exclamation_count, caps_word_count, has_personal_pronoun) that can be segmented and compared against sentiment, with two lexical counts (positive/negative_word_count) that merely restate the sentiment focus, and near-useless columns (question_count is near-constant, avg_word_length is opaque and near-constant, raw word_count is overly fine-grained). Several columns support interpretable relationship discovery, but a substantial portion are restatements or non-informative, yielding moderate overall informativeness.
